pr_body:
They are like PrivateNetwork or NetworkNamespacePath, but for IPC
namespacing instead of network namespacing.

Closes #14908.
pr_comments: Could you please split into two commits, the first refactoring the network NS specific functions in generic helpers, and the second adding the new feature?

hmm, what's the usecase for this? I always found IPC namespaces a weird beast, since they don't namespace the IPC objects that actually matter: AF_UNIX and FIFOs. Both of them are typically anchored in the file system (i.e. AF_UNIX sockets in the fs, or named pipes), and thus subject to mount namespaces. or in case of AF_UNIX are in the abstract namespace and namespaced by network namespaces (which is weir,d but is how it is). Or they are referenced by fds (i.e. socketpair() or pipe2() channels) in which case namespacing doesn't apply.

IPC namespaces only applies to POSIX mqueues (which really nobody uses) and SysV IPC (which are terrible, and people shouldn#t really use either).

Hence, so far, we just tried to stay away from explicit IPC namespacing controls. They are implied by nspawn (since there we want to virtualize a system to the level that is possible) and never used by service sandboxing.

So, what is the usecase here? Why would it be a good idea to have these knobs, in particular IPCNamespacePath=? having that points people to this, under the assumption this would actually be useful, but it's not really, it has almost no effect since the stuff is seldom used these days...

> IPC namespaces only applies to POSIX mqueues (which really nobody uses) and SysV IPC (which are terrible, and people shouldn#t really use either).

I wish this was the case :-) Sadly they are both still used, especially in old "enterprise" software that gets ported left and right. I have some such cases at $work, and it's nigh-impossible to get those changed.

I am a lot more OK with PrivateIPC= than with IPCNamespacePath=. But I am not totally against either. I just try to grok what the background of this is, i.e. usecases.

I wonder if we can find better names for these btw, i.e. somehow communicate that in 90% of cases this is not going to do what people think it does...  PrivateLegacyIPC= is probably a bit too strong a naming, but maybe PrivateTraditionalIPC= or so?  PrivateAuxiliaryIPC=? PrivateOldIPC=? PrivateAncillaryIPC=? or maybe at the very least document in detail that this has no effect on all truly useful, common forms of IPC, but only on those niche forms?

Also, I am wondering if the IPC namespacing shouldn't be implied by default by file system namespacing? i.e. AF_UNIX fs sockets are affected by file system namespacing, and they are the most prominent form of IPC, hence maybe the other forms that are mostly niche and/or legacy stuff should just be implicitly be namespaced by that too? i.e. I think a major weakness of the Linux namespace model is that all this namespacing schemes are pretend-independent of each other, but actually aren't... neither in implementation nor philosophically.

There should probably be PrivateIPC=auto or so, which is equal to yes if we have RootDirectory=/RootImage= set, so that it gets the same treatment as AF_UNIX fs namespace sockets

> Could you please split into two commits, the first refactoring the network NS specific functions in generic helpers, and the second adding the new feature?

Working on it now...

> I wonder if we can find better names for these btw, i.e. somehow communicate that in 90% of cases this is not going to do what people think it does... PrivateLegacyIPC= is probably a bit too strong a naming, but maybe PrivateTraditionalIPC= or so? PrivateAuxiliaryIPC=? PrivateOldIPC=? PrivateAncillaryIPC=? or maybe at the very least document in detail that this has no effect on all truly useful, common forms of IPC, but only on those niche forms?

We already have a `RemoveIPC=`.  Maybe we should add some warning in the descriptions of these "IPC" options...

> We already have a `RemoveIPC=`. Maybe we should add some warning in the descriptions of these "IPC" options...

You have a point. But then again, `RemoveIPC=` also applies to slightly less weird forms of IPC, i.e. POSIX shared memory, /dev/shm/... (whch is still flawed, but not thaaat exotic). i.e `RemoveIPC=` applies to more stuff, actually useful stuff than `PrivateIPC=` does...

There is a serious issue: after creating/joining an IPC namespace, [`/dev/mqueue` has to be remounted][1] to work correctly.  It's too late here and I'll try to do this sane tomorrow...

[1]: http://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/0812.2/00855.html

I've added some words regarding the "weirdness" of the IPCs covered by IPC namespace in the man page.  And if `PrivateIPC` or `IPCNamespacePath` is used, mount namespace will be used and a private instance of `/dev/mqueue` will be mounted.
Made changes suggested by @poettering , and rebased the commits.

issue_context.title: systemd.exec: Add PrivateIPC
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I have a scenario where I have to run the same set of applications which communicate using a POSIX message queue. This obviously causes name clashes when running multiple instances of this set of applications.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Run each instance of the set of applications in its own IPC namespace. I imagine this would take the form of a `PrivateIPC` option which would be picked up (automatically?) by `JoinsNamespaceOf`. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I can hack this in manually or modify the applications so they take the message queue to use as an argument. Still, since we support `PrivateNetwork` together with `JoinsNamespaceOf`, adding `PrivateIPC` to that mechanism shouldn't be too hard.

Are there any major blockers that would make adding this feature problematic? It should be doable to make the `setup_netns` function from namespace.h generic so it can handle more than one namespace. We can write more namespace file descriptors to the storage socket (2 when both `PrivateNetwork` and `PrivateIPC` are specified) and have a process read all file descriptors from the socket and enter all of the namespaces read from the socket.

Or we just add `setup_ipcns` next to `setup_netns` with its own storage socket. I'm not sure if there are any more namespace types that would make sense to add support for in the future.
